summary: Pinned model unexpectedly bypassed during dedicated autoscale causing mixed-model responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer LexiSearch reports that requests explicitly pinned to redwood-gpt-4o-v1.2 are intermittently receiving responses from an older canary variant (redwood-gpt-4o-quant-v1). Impact: Mixed-model outputs are causing downstream scoring mismatches and data quality alerts in LexiSearch's ingestion pipeline. Environment: Dedicated pool (lexi-dedicated-pool) in prod-us-east. Instances affected appear to be a subset of the pool during an autoscale event.

Observed behavior:
- Between 2026-03-13T17:22 and 17:45 UTC, ~11% of pinned requests returned tokens that matched the quant variant response profile (shorter sequences, tokenization differences).
- Customer provided request IDs and sample outputs (attached).

Expected behavior:
- Requests pinned to redwood-gpt-4o-v1.2 should always route to that model variant and never fall back to quant variant unless customer pin removed or explicit fallback policy triggers due to a runtime failure.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Create a dedicated capacity job pinned to redwood-gpt-4o-v1.2 in us-east.
2) Send steady traffic (50 req/s) with occasional bursts until autoscaler triggers a +20% scale-up.
3) Observe responses and model metadata in token_trace header.

Logs & evidence:
- Customer request IDs: lexi-req-20260313-001 to lexi-req-20260313-048 (samples attached in ticket).
- Router logs show route decision for many requests as "PIN_MATCH" but several show "ROUTE_FALLBACK: variant-mismatch" with no prior failure recorded.
- Autoscaler timeline: scale-up started 2026-03-13T17:24:15, new nodes became ready at 17:26:02.
- Related support ticket: SUP-4721 (notes about canary fallback behavior)

Attachments: token traces (redacted), router logs snippet, customer sample outputs.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision dedicated pool with pin to redwood-gpt-4o-v1.2
Generate 50 rps sustained with periodic 200 rps bursts until autoscaler adds nodes
Inspect token_trace and tokenization differences in returned headers
Watch router logs for PIN_MATCH vs ROUTE_FALLBACK entries
comments: 2026-03-13T18:00 Ariana Patel (Support): Acknowledged the report and requested samples and router logs from LexiSearch. Asked SRE to look at routing decisions during the scale event. SLA: P1, first response met.

2026-03-13T18:12 Marcus Chen (SRE): Received logs. Early observation: fallback to quant variant appears correlated with node join events. Opening investigation into routing cache and pin-store consistency across nodes.

2026-03-13T19:04 LexiSearch - Jenna Morales (Customer): Provided additional request IDs and noted the issue only started after last night's canary rollout of quant variants. They're seeing scoring differences in ~10% of requests during scale windows.

2026-03-13T21:30 Marcus Chen (SRE): Hypothesis: per-node in-memory pin cache TTL is shorter than routing cache TTL. When new nodes join they consult central store but router cache still contains stale fallback routes from earlier canary experiment. Working with runtime team to reproduce in staging.

2026-03-14T09:15 Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Reproduced in staging with an autoscale-induced node join. Found that the request-router sometimes applies a cached fallback route when the per-request pin metadata was set by a prior request on a different node. Suggested fix: make pin authoritative at edge router and invalidate fallback cache on pin updates.

2026-03-14T12:40 Marcus Chen (SRE): Applied short-term mitigation: increased pin-cache TTL and added conservative cache-bypass for pinned requests in prod for lexi-dedicated-pool. Monitoring for regression. Noted minor increase in router CPU (~2%).
2026-03-14T13:05 Ariana Patel (Support): Notified customer that we applied a mitigation and asked them to continue sending samples. Awaiting confirmation of reduction in mixed-model responses.
2026-03-14T14:22 LexiSearch - Jenna Morales (Customer): Confirmed mixed responses dropped to ~0.5% in latest tranche. Thanks team. Asked about permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Reproduction in staging shows race condition between autoscaler node join and router fallback cache invalidation.

Root cause candidate: fallback route entries were populated during a prior canary run and persisted in router cache. Pin metadata updates were being stored in a per-node cache that was not consulted when a cached fallback entry existed, allowing the cached fallback to override the pin for some requests.

Edge-case: requests arriving within the ~1–2s window when new nodes register are more likely to hit the inconsistent state because router pool includes both old cached entries and fresh node route state.
Telemetry: token_trace header values and router decision logs are sufficient to correlate each misrouted request to a router instance and a 10–30s prior canary event on that router.
Temporary mitigation validated: bypassing fallback cache on any request with explicit pin reduces misroutes but increases CPU and slightly raises latency percentiles.

Longer-term fix proposed: PR to make pin authoritative at the ingress router, persist pin state in central store with immediate cache invalidation hooks on pin changes, and add tests for autoscale join scenarios. See PR: github.com/redwood-inference/route-fix/pull/201.
resolution_summary: Mitigation applied: router now bypasses fallback cache for pinned requests in lexi-dedicated-pool; customer reports issue largely resolved. Engineering has an in-progress patch to make pin authoritative and to add cache-invalidation hooks. Target for code roll: 2026-03-18 behind feature flag. Postmortem and permanent fix planned after deploy.
next_steps: Merge and canary PR #201 to route-fix repo and monitor (Eng lead: Priya Rao)
Add automated integration test covering autoscale join + pinning scenario (QA)
Postmortem document and runbook updates for model pinning behavior in confluence.runbooks (Owner: Marcus Chen)
Customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-15 to review root cause and timeline
